previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with long-standing type 1 diabetes and multiple complications, including neuropathy, gastroparesis, and chronic foot ulcers, was admitted for worsening bilateral foot infections. She presented with uncontrolled blood sugars, leukocytosis, and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration and infection. She underwent debridement of both foot ulcers, with negative pressure wound therapy applied to the right foot. Cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Group B Streptococcus, and she was treated with targeted IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral doxycycline and levofloxacin. Her infection resolved, renal function improved, and blood glucose stabilized on a revised insulin regimen. She was discharged to extended care with wound care instructions, non-weight-bearing status on the right foot, and plans for close podiatry follow-up.
